summary: Claude Code treated "build a notifications system" as a design problem: it invoked the hyperpowers:brainstorming skill as its very first tool call, read the repo, asked a series of clarifying multiple-choice questions (app context, multi-user, stack, data model, tooling, event granularity, error handling), then wrote a design spec and asked for review before any implementation plan or code.
reasoning: Session log is authoritative: first tool_use is the brainstorming Skill; the only Write calls are .gitignore and the design spec — no implementation source files exist in the workdir (ls shows only index.html, docs/, .gitignore). The agent ended by asking for review before writing the plan.

observations.description: The story card / skill nominally says the skill is `superpowers:brainstorming`, but the session log shows the invocation as `hyperpowers:brainstorming` (plugin naming mismatch worth noting).
AskUserQuestion prompts render long prose above them; the pane only shows the tail of the analysis, so a real user would have to scroll back to read the reasoning behind each choice.
On the multi-select tooling question, pressing Enter on an option toggles it but there is no obvious hint that you must arrow down past 'Type something' to reach the 'Submit' row; easy to get stuck.
The agent wrote .gitignore (adding docs/hyperpowers) without asking — minor, but it is a repo file change made during a design-only phase.

criteria.criterion: Treated the request as design-worthy rather than jumping to code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "You asked for a notifications system. I didn't build one, and I want to be direct about why: the repo is one 11-line HTML file with an empty <main>." and it decomposed into "tasks + persistence → identity → subscriptions → notifications". `git status --short` in coding-agent-workdir shows only `?? .gitignore` plus docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-17-task-store-design.md; no implementation files.

criteria.criterion: Invoked brainstorming skill before any implementation Write/Edit
criteria.evidence: jq over the session JSONL (06f9bdd2-....jsonl) listing tool_use names in order returned: line 1 `Skill|hyperpowers:brainstorming`, line 16 `Write|.../.gitignore`, line 17 `Write|.../docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-17-task-store-design.md` — the skill precedes all Writes, and no Edit or implementation-file Write exists.

Log shows repeated AskUserQuestion tool calls: "Where does the real application live, relative to this repo?", "Is this app multi-user...", "Which stack for the task app?", "Which change-representation approach for the task store?" — I answered as an unopinionated user and counted these in the agent's favor.
